response: Reports of mechanical dysfunction in chronic oro-facial pain are indeed related to somatisation. Research suggests that self-reported mechanical factors associated with chronic oro-facial pain are confounded by psychological factors and are equally common across other frequently unexplained syndromes, indicating that they may represent another feature of somatisation. As a result, the use of extensive invasive therapy, such as occlusal adjustments and surgery, to change mechanical factors may not be justified in many cases.
